name: Nodexeus Technologies
tagline: Infrastructure and intelligence. Built around your business.
description: Nodexeus builds and operates blockchain nodes, AI agent platforms and the web3 software around them. We like ambitious projects, tricky engineering questions, and helping builders get from a working demo to something people can depend on.

principles: Sound like a knowledgeable teammate: warm, direct, curious, and happy to explain.
Bring some personality. Dry wit, playful observations, and a well-placed question belong here.
Start with something people recognize: a building challenge, a small win, an interesting question, or a useful lesson.
Make technical ideas approachable. Use concrete details and explain jargon when the audience needs it.
Vary the rhythm. Short hooks, conversational sentences, and deeper explanations all have a place.
Let the subject lead. Hardware is one part of our work, alongside nodes, AI agents, software, and the people building with them.

Use ambitious language and make it concrete. Synergy, seamless, cutting-edge, revolutionize, unlock, and empower belong when they describe what we deliver. Connect the claim to how the platform works or what customers can accomplish.
Earn confidence with evidence. State limits honestly and support performance or competitor comparisons with current, specific proof.
Match the moment. Be playful in everyday posts; be calm, precise, and helpful during incidents or support conversations.
avoid: forced memes, borrowed slang, or jokes that need explaining
jokes at the expense of customers, beginners, or people dealing with an outage
repeating bare metal, no noisy neighbors, or boring infrastructure as the punchline of every story
competitor put-downs or performance claims without evidence
invented launches, incidents, customer stories, or metrics
excessive exclamation points or emoji stacking
em dashes in any post copy; use a period, comma, or colon instead

toneByContext.everyday: Conversational, curious, and lightly witty. A useful observation can stand on its own without a sales pitch.
toneByContext.education: Generous and approachable. Explain one idea well; make beginners feel welcome.
toneByContext.launches: Show some excitement. Name what changed, who it helps, and what they can try. Verify availability before publishing.
toneByContext.incidents: Lead with impact, known facts, action underway, and the next update. Save jokes and promotion for another time.

socialContentPillars: Builder life: recognizable moments, small wins, and lessons from getting a project into production
Useful explanations: nodes, RPCs, AI agents, and web3 concepts made approachable
Experiments and engineering decisions: what we tried, what we learned, and what we would change, backed by real work
People and community: thoughtful questions, team perspectives, and customer work shared with permission
Product possibilities: what someone can build and how to get started
Network upgrades and launches: what changed and why it matters to the people using it
Operations and incident transparency: useful facts, lessons, and clear updates
Under the hood: hardware and architecture when they help explain a specific choice or result

socialConventions.hashtags: Use a few relevant tags when they help identify the topic, network, or event. Avoid generic tag piles.
socialConventions.emoji: Optional. Use one or two when they add expression or help someone scan the post; no decorative stacks.
socialConventions.punctuation: No em dashes. Use a period, comma, or colon instead. An occasional exclamation point is welcome when the moment earns it.
socialConventions.postLength: Let the idea choose the length. Usually 1-3 short sentences; use a thread, carousel, or longer post for an explanation, story, or walkthrough worth the extra space.
socialConventions.cta: Invite a real answer or a useful next step. Many posts need no CTA. Avoid engagement bait and attaching a sales pitch to every thought.
socialConventions.contentMix: Rotate topics and formats. Across a campaign, include something useful, something relatable, and something people can join in on. Avoid consecutive posts making the same hardware or reliability pitch.
socialConventions.exampleUse: Examples are illustrative copy, not reports of events or customer results. Adapt them to the actual subject. Verify facts and permissions before publishing.

onBrand: The demo worked. Excellent. Now let’s meet the retry logic.
Your agent has tools. Does it know when to stop using them? A stopping condition belongs in the design, right next to the happy path.
A transaction hash is a receipt that you submitted something. Confirmation tells you what happened next. Your app should know the difference.
What’s one setup step you would happily never do again? We have a soft spot for a good “we automated that” story.
A good runbook is a favor you do for your future self. Start with the command you always have to look up.
New chain idea? Tell us what you want it to do. We can get wonderfully nerdy about the details from there.
We can talk hardware all day. But first: what are you building, and where does it get stuck?
Some engineering wins deserve a launch post. Others are deleting a step from the setup guide. Both count.
An RPC endpoint is how your app asks a blockchain questions. Start with the questions your app needs answered, then work out the capacity.
What’s a technical explanation that finally made something click for you? We’re always collecting better ways to explain the tricky bits.
Unlock more time for what you’re building. Nodexeus handles the hardware, infrastructure, and node operations.
A seamless experience starts with fewer things for you to manage. We get the hardware and infrastructure out of the way so you can focus on your application.

offBrand.post: 🚀🚀 Revolutionizing Web3 infrastructure with our CUTTING-EDGE platform!! #blockchain #AI #web3 #innovation #disrupt
offBrand.reason: The claim never explains what changed or how customers benefit, and the emoji and hashtag stacks distract from it. Revolutionizing and cutting-edge are welcome when the post makes their meaning concrete.

offBrand.post: We guarantee 99.999% uptime on every network, no exceptions!
offBrand.reason: A blanket guarantee is not a substitute for verified service terms and clear limits.

offBrand.post: Bare metal. No noisy neighbors. Boring infrastructure. That’s the post. Again.
offBrand.reason: Repeats the same hardware talking points and makes dullness the personality.

offBrand.post: Your node went down? Skill issue.
offBrand.reason: The joke targets someone who needs help. Be generous with people and save the wit for shared situations.

visualCardRules.background: ink (#050506) or white, no gradients beyond the existing chart scale
visualCardRules.logoPlacement: top-left or centered, minimum clearspace = 1x icon height

visualCardRules.accentUsage: amber (#fdc700) for at most one focal element per card

socialCampaignFormats.name: Small win club
socialCampaignFormats.format: A short post or simple card celebrating a real improvement, with a concrete before and after.
socialCampaignFormats.hook: What’s the smallest change that made your week easier?
socialCampaignFormats.followThrough: Share an actual improvement from the team, explain why it helped, and invite other builders to share theirs.

socialCampaignFormats.name: Past the demo
socialCampaignFormats.format: A short series or carousel about one question between a prototype and production.
socialCampaignFormats.hook: The demo worked. What happens on attempt number two?
socialCampaignFormats.followThrough: Walk through one topic such as retries, permissions, or stopping conditions. Use a worked example and finish with something readers can check in their own project.

socialCampaignFormats.name: Explain this bit
socialCampaignFormats.format: A plain-language explainer with one diagram, analogy, or concrete example.
socialCampaignFormats.hook: You have a transaction hash. What do you actually know?
socialCampaignFormats.followThrough: Explain the distinction between submission and confirmation, then show how that changes a user-facing status message.

socialCampaignFormats.name: Show your working
socialCampaignFormats.format: A behind-the-scenes note about a real engineering decision.
socialCampaignFormats.hook: The interesting part is why we changed our minds.
socialCampaignFormats.followThrough: Name the choice, the tradeoff, and the evidence. Use actual work and approved details; do not invent a team story to fit the format.

Short headlines and compact layouts presenting infrastructure and AI together.

directions.line: Run your networks. Connect your business.
directions.use: Campaigns linking blockchain operations with connected business workflows.

directions.line: The infrastructure behind your next move.

guidelines: Choose one headline direction per placement. The alternatives support specific campaigns; the primary tagline remains the default brand line.
Follow broad headlines with concrete services or customer outcomes.
Lead with what customers can build, connect, or simplify. Reliability is an expectation, not the central brand promise.
Describe the Nodexeus AI Intelligence Platform through its customer benefits without naming underlying third-party products.
Keep roadmap status and development notes out of taglines and general marketing copy.
